question: After RFC 0018 is accepted, should OpenClaw own these four opt-in hosting profiles, runtime activation identity, and release-blocking packaged conformance as its initial support contract?
rationale: The profile catalog, identity semantics, security predicates, and release-support obligation are durable product and policy choices that cannot be inferred safely from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Keep Draft Pending Readiness
options.body: Accept the layering direction but defer RFC acceptance until RFC 0018 lands, security predicates are reviewed, and inspectable upgrade proof is attached.

options.title: Narrow The V1 Contract
options.body: Standardize only the least controversial profiles and defer activation identity, node-mode, or release-blocking conformance to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Decline Standard Profiles
options.body: Keep readiness criteria operator-selected and avoid an OpenClaw-owned named posture catalog and conformance promise.

recommendation.title: Keep Draft Pending Readiness
recommendation.body: Accept the layering direction but defer RFC acceptance until RFC 0018 lands, security predicates are reviewed, and inspectable upgrade proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is repeated ownership of Gateway lifecycle, auth, and runtime behavior affected by this support contract.
